title: Barendregt–Geuvers–Klop conjecture
formal: For every pure type system (S,A,R) defined below, does weak normalization of every typable term imply strong normalization of every typable term?

definitions: S is a set of sorts, A⊆S×S is a set of axioms, and R⊆S×S×S is a set of product rules. Terms are finite expressions t ::= x | s | t u | λx:B.t | Πx:B.C, with s∈S and variables from a countably infinite set, modulo renaming bound variables. A context is a finite sequence of declarations of distinct variables. Typing is the least relation Γ⊢t:B generated by the following rules. Axiom: ∅⊢s:t when (s,t)∈A. Start: Γ,x:B⊢x:B when Γ⊢B:s and x is fresh. Weakening: Γ,x:C⊢t:B when Γ⊢t:B, Γ⊢C:s and x is fresh. Product: Γ⊢Πx:B.C:s₃ when Γ⊢B:s₁, Γ,x:B⊢C:s₂ and (s₁,s₂,s₃)∈R. Abstraction: Γ⊢λx:B.t:Πx:B.C when Γ,x:B⊢t:C and Γ⊢Πx:B.C:s for a sort s. Application: Γ⊢t u:C[u/x] when Γ⊢t:Πx:B.C and Γ⊢u:B. Conversion: Γ⊢t:C when Γ⊢t:B, Γ⊢C:s and B=βC. All substitutions avoid capture. A beta step contracts (λx:B.t)u to t[u/x] at any subterm, including inside annotations and product types. =β is the reflexive, symmetric, transitive closure of those steps. A term is typable if Γ⊢t:B for some finite Γ,B. Weak normalization means that each typable term has some finite beta-reduction sequence ending in a term with no beta redex. Strong normalization means that no typable term starts an infinite beta-reduction sequence. Both predicates quantify over open as well as closed terms and over all their reduction choices. The sets S,A,R need not be finite, decidable or functional.

sentences: A pure type system specifies a typed lambda calculus through a uniform collection of formation rules.
Weak normalization means that every well-typed term has some terminating reduction path.
The conjecture asks whether that global property forces every reduction path of every well-typed term to terminate.
A term may have both a normalizing route and a divergent route in less constrained rewriting settings, so the type-system hypothesis is essential.
A proof would connect existence of normal forms with unrestricted evaluation termination across a broad family of typed calculi.
